Subject: Managed Observability: SOW, runbook & pilot schedule (SignalWorks + Nimbus)

Hi Alice, Chris —

Thanks again for taking time last week. Per our call, attached is a draft Shared SOW (RW-SSOW-v1.2.pdf) and a first-pass runbook (managed-observability-runbook-draft.md) that maps responsibilities between SignalWorks (managed services), Nimbus (customer), Datadog (platform), and Redwood (inference telemetry).

High-level ask: could you review the SOW sections highlighted in yellow (Operational Scope, Escalation SLA, and Data Retention)? We want to lock the pilot scope and a 6-week acceptance window.

Key items in this draft:
- Pilot scope: 3 services (inference latency dashboards, tokenization telemetry, KV-cache error tracing)
- Delivery milestones: Kickoff (week 0), Data collection + instrumentation (w1–w2), Integration + dashboards (w3), Acceptance testing (w5–w6)
- SLAs: 99.5% telemetry collection availability; 200ms dashboard refresh SLA for sampled dashboards
- Ownership: SignalWorks runs the managed service; Redwood implements the instrumentation hooks and provides export adapters; Datadog hosts dashboards/alerting.

Attachments: RW-SSOW-v1.2.pdf (SOW), managed-observability-runbook-draft.md (runbook), integration-test-plan.xlsx (test plan).

Immediate asks:
1) Alice/SignalWorks — any redlines to the operational responsibilities?
2) Chris/Nimbus — confirm target systems and retention policy (90 days default?)
3) Marissa/Ben — validate pricing line items and procurement timeline so we can send a final SOW next week.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Managed Observability: SOW, runbook & pilot schedule (SignalWorks + Nimbus)

Jordan —

Thanks for the SOW. Quick notes after first pass:
- SignalWorks comfortable with the pilot scope but we want the definition of "KV-cache error tracing" tightened (specific events and sampling rates).
- Escalation SLA: request a 4-hour P1 acknowledgement (not full resolution) and a 24-hour P1 resolution target for pilot period — we can revisit for production.
- Data retention: Nimbus asked about 365-day cold retention for compliance; for pilot we can do 90 days but need an option to expand.

I've highlighted suggested edits in the PDF and left comments in the runbook draft where we need clearer playbook steps for Datadog alerts. We can incorporate those and share back.

Also want to propose a joint tabletop exercise in week 4 to validate the escalation paths. That helped us surface edge cases in prior integrations.

I'll schedule a 30-min review with Marissa and Jordan if that works — proposed times next Tue/Wed.

Best,
Alice Chen
Head of Partnerships, SignalWorks

Subject: Re: Managed Observability: SOW, runbook & pilot schedule (SignalWorks + Nimbus)

Jordan / team —

Thanks — reviewed the SOW and runbook. A few Redlines / proposals:

1) Operational definitions
- KV-cache error tracing: specify the three event classes we will surface (cache_miss_rate spikes, kv_marshal_errors, eviction_retry_failures) and default sampling at 1% for production but 10% during pilot for diagnostic purposes.

2) SLA adjustments
- Pilot: 4-hour P1 acknowledgement, 24-hour P1 resolution target (SignalWorks asked for this; Redwood accepts for pilot only).
- Production: keep 99.9% telemetry availability target with a 2-hour P1 ack and 12-hour P1 resolution.

3) Acceptance criteria
- Define acceptance as: (a) telemetry coverage >= 95% for listed services during a 48-hour window; (b) successful execution of two simulated incident runbooks in tabletop exercise.

4) Pricing appendix (draft numbers) — see attached pricing rows in integration-test-plan.xlsx. Pilot fixed fee: $40k; optional 365-day retention add-on: $8k/month.

5) Next steps
- Ben: please confirm HubSpot deal id and procurement notes (I left a comment in the SOW PDF).
- Jordan: schedule tabletop exercise wk4; invite Datadog partner success to observe.

I'll incorporate these into RW-SSOW-v1.3 and send back by Thu COB.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
